# Moneo's self-hosted backend: Postgres plus the open-source Supabase services the app talks to
# (Auth, PostgREST, Storage), behind one gateway. Every port binds to 127.0.0.1 only, and
# `npm run setup` writes fresh secrets to .env, which Compose reads for the ${...} values.
# Image versions match Supabase CLI 3.0.0.
name: moneo

services:
  db:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgres:17.11.0.011
    restart: unless-stopped
    command: ["postgres", "-c", "config_file=/etc/postgresql/postgresql.conf", "-c", "log_min_messages=fatal"]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_HOST: /var/run/postgresql
      POSTGRES_USER: supabase_admin
      POSTGRES_DB: postgres
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?run npm run setup}
      PGPASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET:?run npm run setup}
      JWT_EXP: 3600
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:${DB_PORT:-54322}:5432"]
    volumes:
      - ./docker/db/roles.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init-scripts/99-roles.sql:ro
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "postgres", "-h", "localhost"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  auth:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/gotrue:v2.197.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      API_EXTERNAL_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1
      GOTRUE_API_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      GOTRUE_API_PORT: 9999
      GOTRUE_DB_DRIVER: postgres
      GOTRUE_DB_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://supabase_auth_admin:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      GOTRUE_SITE_URL: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      GOTRUE_URI_ALLOW_LIST: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}
      GOTRUE_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
      GOTRUE_JWT_EXP: 3600
      GOTRUE_JWT_AUD: authenticated
      GOTRUE_JWT_DEFAULT_GROUP_NAME: authenticated
      GOTRUE_JWT_ADMIN_ROLES: service_role
      # The one owner account is created by setup; nobody can sign up.
      GOTRUE_DISABLE_SIGNUP: "true"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_EMAIL_ENABLED: "true"
      GOTRUE_MAILER_AUTOCONFIRM: "true"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_PHONE_ENABLED: "false"
      GOTRUE_EXTERNAL_ANONYMOUS_USERS_ENABLED: "false"
      GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_ROTATION_ENABLED: "true"
      GOTRUE_SECURITY_REFRESH_TOKEN_REUSE_INTERVAL: 10
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9999/health"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  rest:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/postgrest:v16.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      PGRST_DB_URI: postgresql://authenticator:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      PGRST_DB_SCHEMAS: public,graphql_public
      PGRST_DB_EXTRA_SEARCH_PATH: public,extensions
      PGRST_DB_MAX_ROWS: 1000
      PGRST_DB_ANON_ROLE: anon
      PGRST_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}

  storage:
    image: public.ecr.aws/supabase/storage-api:v1.88.0
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://supabase_storage_admin:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/postgres
      ANON_KEY: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY}
      SERVICE_KEY: ${SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY}
      AUTH_JWT_SECRET: ${JWT_SECRET}
      STORAGE_BACKEND: file
      FILE_STORAGE_BACKEND_PATH: /var/lib/storage
      FILE_SIZE_LIMIT: 52428800
      TENANT_ID: stub
      GLOBAL_S3_BUCKET: stub
      STORAGE_S3_REGION: local
      ENABLE_IMAGE_TRANSFORMATION: "false"
    volumes: ["storage-data:/var/lib/storage"]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--no-verbose", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1:5000/status"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 40

  # One URL for the app's Supabase client: /auth/v1, /rest/v1 and /storage/v1.
  gateway:
    image: caddy:2.10.2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on: { auth: { condition: service_healthy }, rest: { condition: service_started }, storage: { condition: service_healthy } }
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:${API_PORT:-54321}:8000"]
    volumes: ["./docker/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro"]

volumes:
  db-data:
  storage-data:

// Database checks against the local backend: migration replay with the SQL regressions, then the
// opt-in *.live.test.ts files one at a time (their fixtures lock shared tables). Synthetic data only.
import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { existsSync } from "node:fs";

// Only ever the separate test backend, never the owner's database in .env.
if (!existsSync(".env.qa")) throw new Error("No test backend: run `npm run setup -- --qa` first");
process.loadEnvFile(".env.qa");
const flags = ["RESERVATION", "IMPORT_EXCLUSION", "IMPORT_ROW_UNDO", "VERIFIED_EVIDENCE", "INVESTIGATION_REQUEST"];
const env = { ...process.env, ...Object.fromEntries(flags.map(flag => [`RUN_${flag}_DB_TESTS`, "1"])) };
for (const args of [["supabase/tests/migrations.mjs"], ["node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs", "run", "--no-file-parallelism", ".live.test.ts"]]) {
  const { status } = spawnSync(process.execPath, args, { env, stdio: "inherit" });
  if (status !== 0) process.exit(status ?? 1);
}
# Database checks

These scripts test the SQL functions, row-level security and concurrency of the self-hosted database. They read `SUPABASE_DB_URL` and the Supabase keys from `.env.qa`, the separate test backend (`npm run setup -- --qa`), never the owner's `.env`.

## Migrations and regressions

`npm run test:db` runs the migration replay below and then every opt-in `*.live.test.ts`, one file at a time.

```sh
node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs
```

Replays every migration into a temporary schema, compares it with the current schema (columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers, functions), and runs the `.sql` regression fixtures on both. Everything runs in rollback-only transactions; migration history stays unchanged and the temporary schema is removed.

`workspace-isolation.sql` seeds two synthetic users with records in every application table and checks, as the `authenticated` role, that neither can see or change the other's data. Keep its fixtures and RPC cases in step when adding tables or mutations.

Single regressions run with their `run-*.mjs` script, for example `node supabase/tests/run-goal-reservations.mjs`. `run-sql.mjs` runs the import-review fixture.

## Concurrency

`*-concurrency.mjs` scripts (chat, imports, reviews, recurring occurrences, reservations) open separate authenticated and service connections to check locks, cancellation and duplicate claims. They create synthetic users or a disposable schema, remove them by exact ID, and leave a recovery note in ignored `.qa/` files if interrupted.

## Live checks

- `precision.mjs` reads Money and budget pages through PostgREST with amounts beyond JavaScript's safe integer range.
- `summary-live.mjs` (with the app running) checks scheduled summaries end to end: dispatch, deduplication per period, cancellation and disabling.
- Opt-in unit tests compare SQL with application logic, for example `RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- lib/finance/reservation-balance.live.test.ts` (PowerShell: `$env:RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS='1'` first).

None of these touch the owner's workspace. Migrations themselves are applied by `npm run setup`.

# Database checks

These scripts test the SQL functions, row-level security and concurrency of the self-hosted database. They read `SUPABASE_DB_URL` and the Supabase keys from `.env.qa`, the separate test backend (`npm run setup -- --qa`), never the owner's `.env`.

## Migrations and regressions

`npm run test:db` runs the migration replay below and then every opt-in `*.live.test.ts`, one file at a time.

```sh
node supabase/tests/migrations.mjs
```

Replays every migration into a temporary schema, compares it with the current schema (columns, constraints, indexes, RLS, policies, views, triggers, functions), and runs the `.sql` regression fixtures on both. Everything runs in rollback-only transactions; migration history stays unchanged and the temporary schema is removed.

`workspace-isolation.sql` seeds two synthetic users with records in every application table and checks, as the `authenticated` role, that neither can see or change the other's data. Keep its fixtures and RPC cases in step when adding tables or mutations.

Single regressions run with their `run-*.mjs` script, for example `node supabase/tests/run-goal-reservations.mjs`. `run-sql.mjs` runs the import-review fixture.

## Concurrency

`*-concurrency.mjs` scripts (chat, imports, reviews, recurring occurrences, reservations) open separate authenticated and service connections to check locks, cancellation and duplicate claims. They create synthetic users or a disposable schema, remove them by exact ID, and leave a recovery note in ignored `.qa/` files if interrupted.

## Live checks

- `precision.mjs` reads Money and budget pages through PostgREST with amounts beyond JavaScript's safe integer range.
- `summary-live.mjs` (with the app running) checks scheduled summaries end to end: dispatch, deduplication per period, cancellation and disabling.
- Opt-in unit tests compare SQL with application logic, for example `RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS=1 npm test -- lib/finance/reservation-balance.live.test.ts` (PowerShell: `$env:RUN_RESERVATION_DB_TESTS='1'` first).

None of these touch the owner's workspace. Migrations themselves are applied by `npm run setup`.

- Include source, build, runtime dependency, target-validation, and license-notice metadata in packages.
- Generate per-file archive manifests, SPDX software bills of materials, and GitHub provenance and SBOM attestations.
- Verify uploaded archives against tested checksums and validate the complete draft-release inventory before publication.
- Download and test published release assets in a separate verification workflow.

- Validate binary architecture, endianness, ABI, loaders, and applicable CPU, glibc, and macOS deployment constraints.
- Reject unsafe archive paths and links before extraction.
- Expand relocated-archive tests for timezones, ICU, extensions, compression, PL/Python, JIT, and both Windows archive formats.

- Provide reusable Linux, macOS, and Windows build scripts with [local build instructions](README.md).
- Add scheduled checks for upstream PostgreSQL releases and end-of-life changes.

ENV GOOS=linux

RUN ln -s /usr/local/bin/auth /usr/local/bin/gotrue

ENV GOTRUE_DB_MIGRATIONS_PATH /usr/local/etc/auth/migrations

USER supabase
CMD ["auth"]

.PHONY: all build deps image migrate test vet sec vulncheck format hooks lint unused release
.PHONY: check-gosec check-govulncheck check-oapi-codegen check-staticcheck check-go-version check-format
CHECK_FILES ?= ./...

ifdef RELEASE_VERSION
	VERSION=v$(RELEASE_VERSION)
else
	VERSION=$(shell git describe --tags)
endif

ifneq ($(shell docker compose version 2>/dev/null),)
	DOCKER_COMPOSE = docker compose
else
	DOCKER_COMPOSE = docker-compose
endif

DEV_DOCKER_COMPOSE = docker-compose-dev.yml

BUILD_VERSION_PKG = github.com/supabase/auth/internal/utilities
BUILD_LD_FLAGS = -X $(BUILD_VERSION_PKG).Version=$(VERSION)
BUILD_CMD = go build \
	-o $(1) \
	-buildvcs=false \
	-ldflags "$(BUILD_LD_FLAGS)$(2)"

RELEASE_TARGETS = x86 arm64 darwin-arm64 amd64-strip arm64-strip
RELEASE_ARCHIVES = \
	auth-$(VERSION)-x86.tar.gz \
	auth-$(VERSION)-arm64.tar.gz \
	auth-$(VERSION)-darwin-arm64.tar.gz \
	auth-$(VERSION)-amd64.tar.xz \
	auth-$(VERSION)-arm64.tar.xz

TOOL_BIN_DIR = tools/bin
TOOL_TARGETS = \
	$(TOOL_BIN_DIR)/gosec \
	$(TOOL_BIN_DIR)/staticcheck \
	$(TOOL_BIN_DIR)/govulncheck


help: ## Show this help.
	@awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*?## "} /^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## / {sub("\\\\n",sprintf("\n%22c"," "), $$2);printf "\033[36m%-20s\033[0m %s\n", $$1, $$2}' $(MAKEFILE_LIST)

all: check-go-version vet sec static build ## Run the tests and build the binary.

build: auth auth-amd64 auth-arm64 auth-darwin-arm64 ## Build the binaries.

build-strip: auth-amd64-strip auth-arm64-strip ## Build a stripped binary, for which the version file needs to be rewritten.

	CGO_ENABLED=0 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@),)

auth-x86: deps
	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@),)

auth-amd64: deps
	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@),)

auth-arm64: deps
	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@),)

	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@),)

auth-amd64-strip: deps
	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@), -s)

auth-arm64-strip: deps
	CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 $(call BUILD_CMD,$(@), -s)

deps: ## Install dependencies.
	@go mod download
	@go mod verify

lint: \
go 1.27.0

# Base stage for shared environment setup
FROM node:26-alpine3.24@sha256:c6ad9e9c1d80f6eb607c26b4b0a132ff7a2344fad1c78ea3baa2a7d4c8de6d94 AS base
RUN apk add --no-cache g++ make python3
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json package-lock.json .npmrc ./
COPY scripts/ensure-npm-version.cjs ./scripts/ensure-npm-version.cjs
# The optional `npmrc` build secret lets CI route registry traffic through a
# different registry layer.
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc node scripts/ensure-npm-version.cjs

# Dependencies stage - install and cache all dependencies
FROM base AS dependencies
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm ci --ignore-scripts
# Native addons can use the Node headers already included in the image.
RUN --network=none npm_package_config_node_gyp_nodedir=/usr/local npm rebuild
# Cache the installed node_modules for later stages
RUN cp -R node_modules /node_modules_cache

# Build stage - use cached node_modules for building the application
FROM base AS build
COPY --from=dependencies /node_modules_cache ./node_modules
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Production dependencies stage - prune dev dependencies from cached node_modules
FROM base AS production-deps
COPY --from=dependencies /node_modules_cache ./node_modules

CREATE FUNCTION extensions.pgrst_ddl_watch() RETURNS event_trigger
    LANGUAGE plpgsql
    SET search_path TO 'pg_catalog', 'pg_temp'
    AS $$
DECLARE
  cmd record;
  obj_schema text;
BEGIN
  FOR cmd IN SELECT * FROM pg_event_trigger_ddl_commands()
  LOOP
    -- triggers and rules have no schema of their own (schema_name is NULL),
    -- so use the schema of the table they belong to
    obj_schema := CASE
      WHEN cmd.object_type IN ('trigger', 'rule')
        THEN (pg_identify_object_as_address(cmd.classid, cmd.objid, cmd.objsubid)).object_names[1]
      ELSE cmd.schema_name
    END;

    IF cmd.command_tag IN (
      'CREATE SCHEMA', 'ALTER SCHEMA'
    , 'CREATE TABLE', 'CREATE TABLE AS', 'SELECT INTO', 'ALTER TABLE'
    , 'CREATE FOREIGN TABLE', 'ALTER FOREIGN TABLE'
    , 'CREATE VIEW', 'ALTER VIEW'
    , 'CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW', 'ALTER MATERIALIZED VIEW'
    , 'CREATE FUNCTION', 'ALTER FUNCTION'
    , 'CREATE TRIGGER'
    , 'CREATE TYPE', 'ALTER TYPE'
    , 'CREATE RULE'
    , 'COMMENT'
    )
    -- don't notify in case of CREATE TEMP table or other objects created on pg_temp
    -- also exclude any objects inside Supabase schemas
    AND COALESCE(obj_schema, '') NOT IN ('pg_temp', 'auth', 'realtime', '_realtime', 'storage')
    THEN
      NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema';
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END; $$;

The macOS x86-64 PostgREST binary is only 2.7MB, against roughly 9MB for the arm build, which looks odd. It could be UPX-compressed or broken, and I can't run a Mac here, so I'll flag it as a risk to verify on CI. For mkcert, there are no published digests, so I'll download each binary and compute a sha256 to pin them on first use. I also noticed Next's mkcert.js fetches mkcert into a cache directory, while the desktop shell needs it bundled, so those two paths need reconciling.

Next I'm checking whether Next's mkcert library pulls v1.4.4, which I think it does. Then I'm planning to download the mkcert and postgres archives for every platform to compute and verify their checksums. Since that's a large download, I'll write the fetch script to accept a platform flag or an "all" option, starting with the manifest layout for the Postgres, PostgREST, mkcert, Go, GoTrue, and Storage pins.

I'm writing the backend output layout into desktop/.build, with per-platform folders for postgres, postgrest, gotrue, and mkcert, plus storage-api. Since the desktop shell expects migrations and bootstrap under the resources root, I also need the fetch script to copy those in for dev builds, and I'm weighing who owns that copy step.

I'm settling on platform names as win-x64, mac-arm64, mac-x64, and linux-x64, and having the backend module derive its key from the process platform and architecture, mapping win32-x64 to win-x64 and so on. I'll also have the fetch script sync the migrations on each run so the dev copies don't go stale.

I'm settling on how to pick a platform at runtime and how to unpack the archives. Node has no built-in tar, zip, or xz support, so I'll rely on the system `tar`, which handles most formats on Windows and macOS. On Linux I'll need `unzip` for the zip files.

I'm checking how the tar binary behaves here: Git Bash's GNU tar can't read zip and treats "C:" paths as remote hosts, so on Windows I need to call the System32 bsdtar explicitly. I also want to confirm the Theseus Postgres archives' internal layout before deciding what to prune.

I'm checking the archive contents by listing the downloaded files with `tar -tzf`, which avoids extracting anything, and I'm pulling the mac-arm64 and Linux Postgres builds in the background at the same time.

I'm checking whether fs-xattr is compatible with the setup: it's an N-API, ESM module, and the storage dist is CJS, so I need to see whether require of an ESM module works under the Electron Node version. Recent Node releases support require(esm) by default, so that looks fine. On macOS and Linux, fs-xattr will need a node-gyp build on the host with a C compiler, and since it's N-API it should work with any Node or Electron version. On Windows, I'm thinking about using a shim instead.

I'm settling on a platform split for fs-xattr: rather than building it per platform inside storage-api, I'll replace it with a small dispatcher shim that uses alternate data streams on Windows and loads a native addon on macOS and Linux. The addon path would come from an environment variable set by the backend, which keeps storage-api platform-independent. The catch is that the mac and Linux addon has to be compiled on those systems.

I'm working out how to get the fs-xattr build to run on each platform, and the open question is whether node-gyp is available on the build host. It isn't a dependency of this repo, so I'm looking at pulling in npm's bundled copy or fetching it with npx at build time.

I'm deciding to run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` first and then rebuild fs-xattr alone on non-Windows hosts, so only its native addon gets compiled and copied to a per-platform path. The shim would load that addon through the environment variable and mirror fs-xattr's small JavaScript wrapper. I can't test the mac and Linux builds from here, though.

Next I'm checking for other native modules in the storage tree after npm ci, by looking for binding.gyp files, .node binaries, and prebuilds directories. Then I'll write the fetch script, with the shim as a small CommonJS index.js.

I'm working out the fs-xattr shim's behavior on Windows, using NTFS alternate data streams. For reading, I'd read the stream file directly, and if it's missing, throw ENODATA when the base file exists and ENOENT otherwise. For writing, I need to check that the base file exists first, since writing to a stream of a missing file would silently create it. I'm also checking whether unlinking a stream works the same way.

I'm checking how the shim's ADS-based attribute calls behave on Windows, and I'm noting that listing streams isn't possible from Node, so that method will just return an empty list or throw.  - If the user asks about "ultrareview" or how to run it, explain that /code-review ultra launches a multi-agent cloud review of the current branch (or /code-review ultra <PR#> for a GitHub PR); /ultrareview is a deprecated alias for the same command. It is user-triggered and billed; you cannot launch it yourself, so do not attempt to via Bash or otherwise. It needs a git repository (offer to "git init" if not in one); the no-arg form bundles the local branch and does not need a GitHub remote.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `C:\Users\mgsuk\.claude\projects\C--codebases-Moneo\memory\`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: <short-kebab-case-slug>
description: <one-line summary, used to decide relevance during recall>
metadata:
  type: user | feedback | project | reference
---

<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.
