content.text:
Everything you asked for works on Windows x64: the backend starts under plain Node, passes every smoke check, and passes all 53 SQL regression files. Two parts needed patches you should approve. Storage-api's file backend uses a native module that won't install on Windows, and GoTrue doesn't compile for Windows as published. Nothing is committed, the probe container is removed, and I left the shell agent's running `Moneo.exe` smoke alone.

## Decisions for you
1. **Storage-api on Windows.** Its file backend imports `fs-xattr`, a native module marked `os: ["!win32"]`, so it can't install or run on Windows. I replaced it with a small stand-in, `scripts/desktop/backend-fs-xattr-shim`:
   - On Windows it keeps file metadata in NTFS alternate data streams. This is proven: content type survived upload, download, backup and restore.
   - On macOS/Linux it loads upstream's own addon (N-API), built per platform. That path is untested.
   - The alternative is patching or forking Storage.
2. **GoTrue on Windows.** v2.197.0 fails to compile because of one `unix.SO_REUSEPORT` call in `cmd/serve_cmd.go`. For the Windows target only, a `go build -overlay` drops that call; the source and other platforms stay upstream.
3. **supautils stand-in.** Without supautils, `postgres` gets `must be owner of table objects` on Moneo's storage policy migration (`202609260001_initial.sql`). I reproduced this. During Moneo's migrations only, `postgres` is granted `supabase_auth_admin` and `supabase_storage_admin` (inherit true, set false). It's revoked right after and again at every start; the smoke run confirms nothing stays granted. Otherwise `postgres` keeps the image's `NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS`.

## Smoke and regression results (Windows, Node 22.23.2)
`node scripts/desktop/backend-smoke.mjs` on the final code:
- **Startup:** first start ready in 29.8 s, restart in 6.8 s.
- **Upgrade:** starting a database one migration behind took an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup, then all 121 of 121 migrations were applied.
- **Extensions:** pgcrypto works (sha256 matched Node's, bcrypt) and so does pg_trgm (similarity 0.333).
- **RLS:** through PostgREST the owner sees its workspace and anon sees none.
- **Storage:** a 200,030-byte upload and download through the gateway kept `text/csv`; anon was refused (400).
- **Backup/restore:** backup (1252 KB dump), then restore into a fresh home kept the same owner, workspace, file and content type.
- **Newer database:** a database with a future migration is refused, and Postgres is stopped again.
- **Stop:** each stop ended all 4 processes (GoTrue, Storage, PostgREST, Postgres) and closed the ports.

SQL regressions, run from a temp directory with its own `.env.qa` (the repo's `.env.qa` and `moneo-qa` untouched):
- `supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`: `PASS: fresh replay 121 migrations and 53 SQL regressions` and `PASS: 121 migrations, 0 pending upgrades, 53 SQL regressions; … match`.
- One file at a time: all 53 pass.
- I did not compare against Docker. That would need my own reference stack, and `moneo-qa` was off-limits.

Next sanity check: `next dev -p 3311 -H 127.0.0.1` with the backend's env returned `GET / 200` twice (cold 75 s, then 3.2 s). The owner was signed in automatically and GoTrue recorded sessions. I stopped only the processes I started; git status was unchanged by the run.

## Pinned sources and licenses
Versions and sha256 are in `PINS` in `scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs`.

| Component | Source | License |
|---|---|---|
| PostgreSQL 17.11 | theseus-rs/postgresql-binaries 17.11.1 | PostgreSQL |
| PostgREST v16.5 | GitHub release | MIT |
| GoTrue v2.197.0 | supabase/auth source, built with Go 1.27.0 (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) | MIT |
| Storage API v1.88.0 | supabase/storage source | Apache-2.0 |
| mkcert v1.4.4 | GitHub release | BSD-3-Clause |

I chose theseus over zonky because zonky has no `pg_dump`, `pg_restore` or `psql`. The theseus builds bundle dependency notices and provenance files.

## Sizes

| Platform | Postgres (pruned) | PostgREST | GoTrue | mkcert | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| win-x64 (built) | 63.2 MB | 62.3 MB | 36.5 MB | 4.7 MB | 166.7 MB |
| linux-x64 | ≈75 MB (estimated) | 19.6 MB | 35.6 MB | 4.6 MB | ≈135 MB |
| mac-arm64 | ≈68 MB (estimated) | 70.9 MB | 34.0 MB | 4.9 MB | ≈178 MB |
| mac-x64 | ≈67 MB (estimated) | 17.4 MB | 36.6 MB | 5.1 MB | ≈126 MB |

Storage API adds 344.8 MB on every platform. Its only remaining native files are `@datadog/pprof` prebuilds, used only by its profiler code path.

## Other differences from the Supabase image
- Not bundled: supautils, safeupdate, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, vault/pgsodium, pg_stat_statements, realtime; no Moneo migration needs them. Without safeupdate, a PostgREST DELETE/UPDATE with no filter is not rejected (RLS still limits it).
- `uuid-ossp` is missing from the Windows Postgres build, so the bootstrap creates it only where available. Nothing in Moneo, GoTrue or Storage uses it.
- Postgres keeps the image settings that change results (UTC, `extra_float_digits=0`, `row_security`, ICU en-US collation). It sets `jit=off` and uses the default `wal_level`.

## Open risks
- **MSVC runtime on Windows:** Postgres imports `vcruntime140.dll`, `vcruntime140_1.dll` and `msvcp140.dll`, which Windows doesn't ship. The packaging needs to bundle them app-local or run vc_redist.
- **macOS PostgREST** links Homebrew's libpq by absolute path (`/opt/homebrew/...` on arm64, `/usr/local/...` on x64). The script now relinks it with `install_name_tool` plus an ad-hoc signature, but only on a mac host, so this is untested. All macOS binaries still need hardened-runtime signing and notarization.
- **Not run on macOS or Linux at all.** Their Postgres archives contain symlinks that Windows can't extract, so they have to be fetched on CI. PostgREST, GoTrue and mkcert did cross-build for all three from here.
- **Node version:** Storage declares `node >=26` and I tested only Node 22. Electron's Node version needs checking.
- **Restore is not crash-atomic.** It first takes a `before-restore` backup, so the old state is recoverable.

## Contract additions
All optional, so the brief's contract still holds:
- `startBackend(paths, progress, { fork, appUrl, appVersion })`. The default `fork` uses Electron's `utilityProcess` when running inside Electron.
- `backup(paths, reason, { automatic })`. The newest 5 automatic backups are kept.

Default ports are 54331 (gateway) and 54332 (database); if busy, a free port is picked and saved. `.gitignore` got two appended lines (`/desktop/.cache/`, `/desktop/.build/`). I need no new dependencies; `esbuild` is already in `node_modules`.

Files are in `desktop/src/backend/`:
- `index.ts`
- `config.ts`
- `postgres.ts`
- `processes.ts`
- `gateway.ts`
- `migrations.ts`
- `backup.ts`
- `README.md`

Files in `desktop/bootstrap/`:
- `00-roles.sql`
- `10-schema.sql`

Files in `scripts/desktop/`:
- `fetch-backend.mjs`
- `backend-load.mjs`
- `backend-run.mjs` (runs the backend in the foreground for dev)
- `backend-smoke.mjs`
- `backend-fs-xattr-shim/`

content:
Thanks — reviewed and committed (f6e9fc3d on branch t3/desktop-app-pwa, draft PR #194). I approve all three deviations (fs-xattr shim, Windows GoTrue overlay, temporary migration-only grants). The shell agent integrated your module; the packaged Windows app loads Home with your backend. Follow-ups, same file ownership as before (plus you may edit desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs ONLY for adding the extra resource files these need; do not commit, I integrate):
1. Orphans after a hard kill: when Electron is force-killed, postgres (and possibly gotrue/postgrest/storage) keep running. On startBackend, recover: record child PIDs + executable paths in home/run/; on next start terminate only recorded processes whose PID is alive AND whose executable path is inside our resources dir (verify before killing; never kill by name), and if postmaster.pid points to a live postgres for our data dir, stop it with pg_ctl stop -m fast before starting. Prove it in backend-smoke.mjs (kill the parent Node runner hard, then start again in the same home: works, no duplicate processes).
2. content.thinking:
I'm noting that the redistribution license itself doesn't grant rights to ship the extracted DLLs. Instead, app-local deployment would rest on the Visual Studio "Distributable Code" terms and REDIST.TXT, which Microsoft's docs describe as copying the files into the application's own folder. Those rights belong to Visual Studio licensees, so I'm checking whether that applies here.

I'm weighing whether the app-local route holds up legally: the Visual Studio Distributable Code terms and REDIST.TXT cover shipping these DLLs, but only for maintainers who hold a Visual Studio license, and the signed binaries from the extraction should match Microsoft's own. The per-user installer lacks the elevation that running the redist installer silently would need, so app-local is the practical path.

I'm going to fetch the VC++ redist and pull the DLLs out of it, using the pinned SHA-256 and parsing the Burn manifest to find the vcRuntimeMinimum cab rather than scanning for cab headers. Extraction needs bsdtar on Linux since GNU tar can't handle cab files, and I'll warn if it's missing. After extracting, I'll check each DLL against the three pinned hashes and place them in postgres/bin, since the loader searches the exe's own directory first and that's where the extension DLLs will find vcruntime140.dll.

I'm checking whether the Windows DLLs will resolve correctly, since libpq and the initdb/pg_ctl/pg_dump tools can find the bundled vcruntime140.dll through the app directory or PATH. content.thinking:
I've confirmed the "use strict" placement after the banner is harmless, since strict mode doesn't apply there anyway. Next I'm updating the smoke test for orphaned processes: spawning the backend runner as a child with a fixed home directory, waiting for its env file, then recording the services and postmaster PID before force-killing the runner. The open question is whether killing the runner also takes down its children on Windows, which I expect it won't.

Next I'm checking for orphans after the runner is force-killed: the postmaster, auth, and rest processes should still be alive while storage may exit on its watchdog. Once the backend starts again in the same home, I want to confirm the old PIDs are gone and that every bundled postgres process traces back to the new postmaster, so no duplicates are left running.

Now I'm working out where the orphan check fits in the smoke flow: whether to use a separate home for it or reuse the main one, and how to avoid false positives from other smoke runs sharing the same bundle. My plan is to match postmasters by their data directory and check that old service PIDs are gone and none of the bundle's processes still have the dead runner as parent. Starting with the existing in-process first start, I'd switch to launching via the runner child, then hard-kill it, then do the upgrade start in the same home.

I'm now looking at the pg-format package, which breaks at runtime because its index file calls `require(__dirname + '/reserved.js')`. I plan to fix that with a build plugin that rewrites those requires to relative `./` paths, and to make the rule generic across node_modules rather than specific to this one file.

The runtime-relevant items are `postgres-migrations`, which needs the migrations SQL shipped, `pg-format`, which needs the require rewrite, and `@fastify/swagger`, which reads package.json when docs are exposed. I'm checking the docs setting next.

content.thinking:
I'm trying to work out why GoTrue and PostgREST were killed along with the runner on Windows. My guess is that libuv puts child processes into a job object with kill-on-close set, through a global job handle it creates for the process, so when that job closes everything under it dies.

So on Windows, libuv's kill-on-close job object takes GoTrue and PostgREST down with the runner, while postgres survives because pg_ctl breaks away from the job. That means only postgres should be left behind as an orphan there. I'm thinking the test should be platform-aware, and I still need a way to exercise the stale-PID kill logic for the services on Windows.

I'm now planning a test for the Windows case: postgres should survive as the one orphan, and I'd check whether GoTrue and PostgREST are still alive, expecting them dead there but alive and killed by recovery on Unix. I'm also weighing a check that recovery leaves an unrelated process alone when it's recorded in services.json, and I'm working out how to get a long-running bundle process for that without the usual tools exiting right away.

I'm now restructuring the test: spawn the runner, read the env and postmaster state, kill the runner, then check whether auth and rest survive. I'm also adding two decoy processes recorded in services.json, one that should be killed and one that should be left alone, so the stale-PID logic gets exercised on both platforms.

I'm settling on two decoy processes recorded in services.json: a detached postgrest pointed at a closed database, which recovery should kill, and a detached node process posing as the auth service, which it should leave alone. Once the upgrade start checks those outcomes, I'll kill the sleeper myself. Before that, I need to stop the leftover postgres 19464 from my earlier run with pg_ctl.
On Windows, libuv ties every Node child to a kill-on-close job object, so GoTrue and PostgREST died with the runner while pg_ctl's postgres survived. I'm stopping that leftover postgres now.

# Moneo Desktop native backend

`index.ts` replaces `docker-compose.yml` inside the desktop app: PostgreSQL, GoTrue, PostgREST and the
Storage API run as child processes on `127.0.0.1`, behind a small gateway with the same three paths as
`docker/Caddyfile`. The binaries come from `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs` (pinned versions and
SHA-256 in that script), and land in `desktop/.build/` (in a package, `resources/`).

## Home folder

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `config.json` (0600) | generated secrets (same generation as `scripts/setup.mjs`), preferred ports, setup state |
| `postgres/` | the cluster (`initdb -U supabase_admin`, UTF8, ICU en-US, scram-sha-256) |
| `storage/` | Storage API files |
| `data/`, `workflow/` | `MONEO_DATA_DIR`, `WORKFLOW_LOCAL_DATA_DIR` for the app |
| `backups/<time>-<reason>/` | `database.dump` (pg_dump -Fc), `storage/`, `config.json`, `manifest.json` |
| `logs/` | `backend.log`, `auth.log`, `rest.log`, `storage.log`, `postgres/` |
| `run/services.json` | PIDs of running services, so a start after a crash can end leftovers |

## Start order

1. Postgres (`initdb` on first run, otherwise stale `postmaster.pid` recovery), via `pg_ctl`.
2. First run only: `desktop/bootstrap/*.sql` as `supabase_admin`, then the passwords and JWT settings
   `docker/db/roles.sql` sets.
3. Refuses to go on if the database has a migration newer than the bundled ones. With pending
   migrations (or other bundled service versions) on an existing database: an automatic
   `pre-upgrade` backup (the newest 5 automatic backups are kept).
4. GoTrue (runs its migrations), Storage API (runs its migrations), PostgREST, gateway.
5. `supabase/migrations` exactly like `scripts/setup.mjs` (same `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`,
   one transaction per file, `notify pgrst`), then the owner through the GoTrue admin API.

## Differences from the Docker backend

- **No supautils, safeupdate, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements,
  realtime.** Nothing in Moneo uses them. `authenticator` therefore has no
  `session_preload_libraries`; without safeupdate, a PostgREST `DELETE`/`UPDATE` with no filter is not
  rejected (RLS still limits it to the owner's rows).
- **supautils' policy grants.** In the image, supautils lets `postgres` create and drop policies and
  triggers on `auth.*`/`storage.*` tables it does not own. Moneo's migrations need that
  (`create policy … on storage.objects`). During Moneo's own migrations only, `postgres` is granted
  `supabase_auth_admin` and `supabase_storage_admin` (`inherit true, set false`); the grant is revoked
  right after, and at every start in case a crash interrupted it. `postgres` otherwise keeps the
  image's attributes: `NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS`.
- **uuid-ossp** is created only where the bundled PostgreSQL has it (not in the Windows build).
- **Storage metadata on Windows.** Storage keeps content type, cache control and etag in extended
  attributes through the native `fs-xattr`, which does not exist on Windows. The bundled Storage uses
  `scripts/desktop/backend-fs-xattr-shim`: NTFS alternate data streams on Windows, the upstream
  N-API addon on macOS and Linux.
- **GoTrue on Windows** is built with a `go build -overlay` that drops one `SO_REUSEPORT` call
  (no such option on Windows); see `fetch-backend.mjs`.
- Postgres settings follow the image where they change results (`timezone = UTC`,
  `extra_float_digits = 0`, `row_security = on`, english text search); `jit = off`, no replication
  (`wal_level` default), logs rotate daily for a week.

content.text:
All four follow-ups are done and verified on Windows. The full smoke test and `supabase/tests/migrations.mjs` both pass on the final code. Nothing is committed, `desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs` needed no change (its existing `extraResources` filter already covers the new files), and nothing of mine is left running.

## 1. Leftovers after a hard kill
- **Records:** `run/services.json` now stores PID, executable path and, for Storage, the script path.
- **Next start, before Postgres starts:** a recorded process is ended only if it's alive, its executable is the recorded one, and that executable is inside the bundled backend (resolving junctions). For Storage, the recorded Node/Electron binary must also be running the recorded bundled script. Nothing is matched by name; a PID now used by another program is logged and left alone.
- **Postgres:** if `postmaster.pid` points to a live `postgres` from this bundle, or one whose command line names this data folder, it's stopped with `pg_ctl stop -m fast`. Otherwise the file is stale and is deleted.
- **What actually survives a hard kill on Windows:** only Postgres. libuv puts every child Node spawns into a kill-on-close job object, so GoTrue and PostgREST die with the parent; `pg_ctl`'s server is the one that breaks away. On macOS/Linux GoTrue and PostgREST can survive, and the PID check covers them there (not run on those platforms).
- **Storage** now exits by itself within a second once its parent is gone. A few lines at the top of the bundle watch `MONEO_PARENT_PID`.
- **Proof in the smoke test:** the backend runs in a child `backend-run.mjs`, which is killed hard. Two planted records then show the checks hold on any platform:
  - a detached PostgREST from the bundle, which recovery must end;
  - an unrelated process recorded under GoTrue's path, which it must leave alone.

## 2. MSVC runtime
- **Source:** Microsoft's VC_redist.x64.exe 14.44.35211.0, from its versioned download URL (the path contains its SHA-256, which I pinned). The signature checks as valid (Microsoft).
- **How it's extracted:** the installer is never run. The script reads its embedded cabinets and takes the three DLLs from the runtime package; each DLL is pinned by sha256 and is itself Microsoft-signed (14.44.35211.0).
- **Where they go:** `postgres/bin` and `postgrest/`, plus the runtime's `license.rtf`. They only extract on a Windows (or macOS) host.
- **License basis:** the redist's own license only says "install and use". The right to ship the DLLs app-local comes from Visual Studio's "Distributable Code" terms (REDIST.TXT), which assume the distributor holds a Visual Studio licence (Community/Build Tools count). Worth a quick legal look; the other route is running vc_redist from the installer, which needs admin rights the per-user installer doesn't have.
- **Verified by loaded-module listing:** `postgres` loaded `postgres\bin\vcruntime140.dll`, `msvcp140.dll` and `vcruntime140_1.dll`, and `postgrest` loaded `postgrest\vcruntime140.dll`. That's the app-local copies, even though this machine also has them in System32.

## 3. Storage API size and paths
- It's now an esbuild bundle: `server.js` (12.8 MB) plus pino's three worker files, `migrations/`, `LICENSE`, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt` (492 bundled packages, generated from esbuild's metafile).
- **Total 16.2 MB, 119 files** (was 345 MB). No native modules and no `node_modules`.
- Longest path under `resources\` is 85 chars for Storage and 101 for anything (a GoTrue migration). Under a typical `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Moneo\resources\` that's about 168 absolute.
- Bundling needed three fixes:
  - `pg-format`'s `require(__dirname + '/reserved.js')` is rewritten so it gets bundled.
  - `postgres-migrations`' bootstrap SQL is shipped next to the bundle.
  - Storage now runs with `EXPOSE_DOCS=false`, since Swagger reads a `package.json` the bundle doesn't have. Moneo doesn't use the docs.

## 4. Final runs
`node scripts/desktop/backend-smoke.mjs`:
```
PASS stop ended 4 processes (13408, 11444, 17416, 2652) and closed the ports
PASS force-quit left postgres 36432 running (GoTrue ended, PostgREST ended); Storage exited by itself
PASS recovery ended the old postmaster and the planted bundled PostgREST (31824), and left the unrelated process (9556) alone
PASS after the force-quit: leftovers ended; one postmaster (35848) for this data folder, one GoTrue, one PostgREST
PASS postgres (pid 35848) loaded the app-local MSVC runtime: win-x64\postgres\bin\vcruntime140.dll, win-x64\postgres\bin\msvcp140.dll, win-x64\postgres\bin\vcruntime140_1.dll
PASS postgrest (pid 11728) loaded the app-local MSVC runtime: win-x64\postgrest\vcruntime140.dll
PASS pending migration triggered backup 2026-11-10T21-15-54Z-pre-upgrade
PASS 121 of 121 migrations applied
PASS postgres is NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS like the image, without the migration-time owner roles
PASS pgcrypto (sha256 bb9cc8fd91c6…, bcrypt) and pg_trgm (similarity 0.333, …)
PASS PostgREST: owner sees its workspace 9ae4017a-…, anon sees none (RLS)
PASS Storage: 200030 bytes uploaded and downloaded as the owner with content-type text/csv; anon refused (400)
PASS backup 2026-11-10T21-15-59Z-smoke (1252 KB dump)
PASS stop ended 4 processes (16932, 36268, 11728, 35848) and closed the ports
PASS restored home: same owner, same workspace, same file and content type
PASS stop ended 4 processes (18772, 39780, 30476, 17252) and closed the ports
PASS a database with a newer migration is refused and postgres is stopped again
All backend smoke checks passed.
```
First start is now ready in 15.4 s (was about 30 s); restarts take about 5 s.

`supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`, run against a fresh native backend from a temp folder with its own `.env.qa` (the repo's `.env.qa` and `moneo-qa` untouched):
```
PASS: fresh replay 121 migrations and 53 SQL regressions; disposable schema rollback verified
PASS: 121 migrations, 0 pending upgrades, 53 SQL regressions; columns/constraints/indexes/RLS/policies/views/triggers/functions match; rollback verified
migrations.mjs exit=0
```
Typecheck (`desktop/tsconfig.json`) and eslint on my files pass.

## Changed files
- `desktop/src/backend/processes.ts`, `postgres.ts`, `index.ts`, `README.md`
- `scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs`
- `scripts/desktop/backend-run.mjs` (gained a `--resources` option)
- `scripts/desktop/backend-smoke.mjs`

**Still untested:** the macOS/Linux side of the leftover check (reading process paths there) and the Linux CAB extraction, which needs `bsdtar`. Neither affects the win-x64 build.
